classification.difficultyReason: Keep the explicitly defined whole fixed when comparing choices, distinguishing a quarter-square from one of four squares and eight sevenths from seven eighths.

content.prompt: Choose the diagram that correctly shows:

inlines.text: if the whole is the shaded square shown below.

spec.description: One square; its side length must equal each separate square in A and the outer square in B.
spec.mathematics: The reference area is one whole.

template.shadeReason: The filled square defines one whole.

spec.description: Four separate equal squares with only the second shaded. The template does not express the external choice label and required reference-scale relationship.
spec.mathematics: Each square equals the reference whole, so the shaded area is one whole.
spec.answerVisibility: Option label and shading are permanent; no correctness mark.

spec.description: One reference-sized square split into four vertical strips, with the third shaded. External choice label and equal physical scale are required.
spec.mathematics: One of four equal parts of the given whole.
spec.answerVisibility: Option label and shading are permanent; no correctness mark.

answer.worked:
B divides a square equal to the given whole into four equal strips and shades one. A shades an entire reference-sized square.

Correct answer: B.

inlines.text: if the whole is the shaded seven-cell bar shown below.

spec.description: Seven shaded cells defining one whole. Explicit TikZ preserves the same cell size across the seven- and eight-cell options.
spec.mathematics: Seven equal cells represent one whole.

spec.description: Seven reference-sized cells; the first is unshaded and the other six shaded. External label and shared cell scale require explicit construction.
spec.mathematics: Six sevenths of the reference whole.

spec.description: Two aligned seven-cell bars stacked vertically; the upper is fully shaded and only the sixth cell of the lower is shaded. The template cannot preserve this vertical arrangement and shared reference-cell scale.
spec.mathematics: Eight shaded cells, each one seventh of the reference whole.

spec.description: Eight cells of the same size as the reference cells; only the second is unshaded. Explicit construction preserves its greater total length.
spec.mathematics: Seven shaded cells equal one reference whole.

answer.worked:
The given whole contains 7 equal cells, so each cell represents $\frac17$. B shades $7+1=8$ such cells, representing $\frac87$. A shades 6 cells, and C shades 7 cells.

Correct answer: B.
